flags: The saved byways guide gives 30 minutes driving time; FHWA gives 20 minutes plus stops. The overview explicitly uses FHWA’s estimate.
The cache supports the 1996 designation and river/rail setting but not WV 72’s construction history.
Strip order is Dunkard Bottom, Rowlesburg, Macomber. The third moment is within Rowlesburg; no Macomber page is cached, so an unsupported endpoint description is omitted.

Dunkard Bottom settlement dates conflict: the byways guide gives c. 1754, the Cheat River article 1756, and the dedicated article 1753. The date is omitted. The dedicated article also disputes the historical marker’s names, date and fate of the brothers.

The Dunkard Bottom conflict narrative lacks a cached Indigenous community or primary historical source. Detailed perpetrators, casualty counts and captivity accounts are not used. No surviving settlement structures or access are claimed.
The old byways guide promotes Briery Mountain WMA, but cache/10.txt reports permanent closure for a live-fire range. It is not offered as a visitor stop.
No current factual claims were dropped for lack of cache support. The source’s subjective isolation language was removed rather than presented as a traveler’s experience.

FHWA and the byways guide use Cheat River Canyon for the road scenery; the river article locates the named Cheat Canyon downstream of Albright. Prose uses river canyon for roadside views and does not equate the driving route with the named whitewater reach.
The saved guide does not identify its original issuing publisher in the extracted text. Its reference names the hosting publisher, MH3WV.
